bottleneck.description: Suborbital space-tourism operator (SpaceShipTwo / Delta-class), not a satellite communications provider; no supply-chain bottleneck role — service is a discretionary consumer experience with multiple emerging alternatives (Blue Origin New Shepard, future SpaceX/Polaris).

dependency.key_customers: Private individuals (ticketed astronauts ~$450K/seat), research payload clients (NASA, universities) for microgravity experiments.
dependency.key_suppliers: The Spaceship Company (in-house manufacturing arm), Aurora Flight Sciences/Bell Textron and Qarbon Aerospace for Delta-class production partners, hybrid rocket motor suppliers.

editorial.notes: SPCE is mis-cohorted as satellite communications — it operates a suborbital tourism vehicle with no satcom function. Bottleneck rating is LOW: no supply-chain criticality, tourism is fully substitutable by Blue Origin and other future entrants, and the company has disclosed substantial doubt about ability to continue as a going concern with commercial flights pushed to late 2026. Financial distress flagged separately; structural bottleneck position is weak regardless.
